Count the missing-value codes in SRTR data

Source: R/srtr_missing_report.R
srtr_missing_report.Rd

Reports, for each variable, how many values stand for missing information and of which kind: unknown, not done, not applicable and so on. Nothing in the data is changed. Use it to see what is there before deciding how to handle it.

Usage

srtr_missing_report(
  df,
  cols = NULL,
  file_key = NULL,
  detail = c("type", "code"),
  release = NULL,
  extra_codes = NULL
)

Arguments

df

A data frame from an SRTR SAF file.

cols

Names of the columns to report. NULL (the default) reports every column that missing_codes covers.

file_key

The dataset df comes from, such as "TX_KI". NULL uses the file_key attribute that load_srtr_file() sets. If there is none, variables are looked up by name alone, and a variable whose format differs between datasets is skipped, with a message.

detail

"type" (the default) gives one row per variable and kind of missing value found. "code" gives one row per classified code, including codes that do not occur (n is 0), which shows whether the codes in missing_codes match the data.

release

The SAF release, as in load_srtr_file(). NULL uses the release recorded on df, or else the bundled dictionary.

extra_codes

Your own codes, for values that missing_codes does not cover: a named list with one element per column, each a named character vector giving the type of each value, such as list(MY_VAR = c("9" = "unknown")). These win over missing_codes, and apply alike to raw codes and to labelled columns. If two codes of a format share one label, both must be given the same type.

Value

A tibble with one row per variable and kind of missing value:

variable

The column name.

format

The variable's SRTR format, or NA if it has none.

missing_type

A type from missing_codes, or "not_in_format" for a value the variable's format does not list, or "na" for a value that is already NA.

n

The number of rows.

percent

n as a percentage of all rows of df.

With detail = "code", code and meaning columns identify each code; they are NA in the "not_in_format" and "na" rows. Partly known codes (type "partial") are reported too, although they are not wholly missing.

Details

Codes are recognised from missing_codes, by what they mean in the variable's own format: the same code number can be "Unknown" in one format and an ordinary value in another. Raw codes and labelled columns (from apply_srtr_factors()) give the same counts. Flag columns that have no format are recognised from the variables table of missing_codes, which is not taken from the SRTR dictionary.

The report holds counts, and the codes and meanings that missing_codes lists. It never holds a value taken from the data: values a format does not list are counted together and not shown. Counts from SRTR data can still be small cells; treat them as you would any other table made from the data.

See also

missing_codes, srtr_normalize_missing()

Examples

# Made-up rows using TX_KI column names
df <- data.frame(
  DON_ANTI_CMV = c("P", "N", "U", "ND", NA),
  DON_HIST_DIAB = c(1, 5, 998, 998, 2)
)
srtr_missing_report(df, file_key = "TX_KI")
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>   variable      format  missing_type     n percent
#>   <chr>         <chr>   <chr>        <int>   <dbl>
#> 1 DON_ANTI_CMV  SRLSTT  unknown          1      20
#> 2 DON_ANTI_CMV  SRLSTT  not_done         1      20
#> 3 DON_ANTI_CMV  SRLSTT  na               1      20
#> 4 DON_HIST_DIAB HSTDBDR unknown          2      40
#> 5 DON_HIST_DIAB HSTDBDR partial          1      20
srtr_missing_report(df, file_key = "TX_KI", detail = "code")
#> # A tibble: 8 × 7
#>   variable      format  code  meaning                 missing_type     n percent
#>   <chr>         <chr>   <chr> <chr>                   <chr>        <int>   <dbl>
#> 1 DON_ANTI_CMV  SRLSTT  U     U: Unknown              unknown          1      20
#> 2 DON_ANTI_CMV  SRLSTT  ND    ND: Not Done            not_done         1      20
#> 3 DON_ANTI_CMV  SRLSTT  PD    PD: Pending             pending          0       0
#> 4 DON_ANTI_CMV  SRLSTT  C     C: Cannot Disclose      cannot_disc…     0       0
#> 5 DON_ANTI_CMV  SRLSTT  I     I: Indeterminate        indetermina…     0       0
#> 6 DON_ANTI_CMV  SRLSTT  NA    NA                      na               1      20
#> 7 DON_HIST_DIAB HSTDBDR 998   998: UNKNOWN            unknown          2      40
#> 8 DON_HIST_DIAB HSTDBDR 5     5: YES, DURATION UNKNO… partial          1      20
